newsitem.title: UK: BP says refining margins to remain under pressure.
newsitem.headline: BP says refining margins to remain under pressure.

text.p: British Petroleum Co plc said on Tuesday that its downstream operating profit in the second quarter of 1997 was the best in a decade but that margins fell in July and should remain under pressure.
But the company said there should be some "compensating effects" from both existing marketing activities and the recent entries into new markets.
"Increased revenues and cost savings arising from the Mobil joint venture are expected to become significant later in 1997," BP said.

Looking ahead, BP said its upstream production in the second half of the year should increase compared to the same period last year relecting a build-up in fields that came onstream in 1996 in the Gulf of Mexico and the North Sea and added output in Venezuela, Mexico and Alaska.

BP attributed the buoyant refining and marketing performance in the second quarter to "continuing improvements in both refining and marketing performance, together with a more favourable BP refining environment".
It said its chemicals' result was up by 24 percent in dollar terms over a year ago, "mainly due to increased volumes" and was achieved in spite of a "weaker overall environment".
The oil giant said crude oil demand strength is expected to persist over the next few months although new production and increasing Iraqi exports "may lead to short term price volatility".
